terms.gloss: well, all right; granted, be it so
terms.grammar: future imperative of sum, used alone
evidence: Cic. Div. Caec. 47: estō: ipse nihil est, nihil potest (Lewis & Short s.v. sum)
terms.comment: Granting a point before going on: “well, so be it; but …”.

terms.gloss: well, rather; no indeed (correcting what was just said)
evidence: Plaut. Most. 3.1.19: Etiam fatētur dē hospite? — Immō pernegat. (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: it corrects or sharpens what precedes and is always followed by the corrected statement; it is never a bare “no”.

terms.gloss: why, indeed; nay even (adding something stronger: quīn etiam)
evidence: Cic. Att. 13.26.3: quīn etiam noctibus (Lewis & Short)

sources: Lewis & Short: sum
Lewis & Short: immo
Lewis & Short: quin
Lewis & Short: em
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 405.
